title: Administrative Assistant
description:
Are you an organised, proactive and friendly administrator looking for a flexible part-time opportunity within education? Tradewind Recruitment is currently seeking a reliable and experienced College Administrator to join a busy college in central Hull. This is to start ASAP, is a temporary position, and will initially last until about 18th December 2026.

This is a fantastic opportunity for an administrator who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys supporting students and staff, and takes pride in keeping an educational setting running smoothly.

The Role
- Position: College Administrator
- Location: Central Hull
- Hours: 8:30am-4:30pm
- Working pattern: 2 days per week, with flexibility on which two days
- Pay rate: 15.00- 16.50 per hour, depending on experience and qualifications
- Recruitment agency: Tradewind Recruitment

Key Responsibilities

As a College Administrator, you will play a vital role in the day-to-day running of the college, providing efficient administrative support to teaching staff, students, senior leaders and visitors.

General Administration
- Providing comprehensive administrative support to the college office and wider staff team.
- Managing incoming telephone calls, emails and general enquiries in a professional and friendly manner.
- Welcoming visitors, students, parents and external professionals, ensuring they are directed to the appropriate departments.
- Maintaining accurate records, filing systems and confidential documentation.
- Typing, preparing, formatting and distributing letters, reports, correspondence and other college documents.
- Photocopying, scanning, printing and collating paperwork and teaching resources.
- Managing incoming and outgoing post and deliveries.
- Monitoring office supplies and assisting with ordering stationery and other resources.
- Supporting senior leaders and teaching staff with ad hoc administrative tasks as required.

Student Administration and Attendance
- Recording, monitoring and updating student attendance, lateness and absence information.
- Contacting parents, carers or students regarding unexplained absences, in line with college procedures.
- Processing student admissions, enrolment information, transfers and withdrawals where required.
- Supporting student registration and ensuring relevant documentation is completed accurately.
- Assisting with timetable changes, room bookings and the organisation of student appointments.
- Responding to student queries and directing them to the appropriate member of staff or support service.
- Maintaining confidentiality when handling sensitive student information.

We are looking for someone who:
- Has previous experience in an administrative or reception-based role; experience within a school, college or other educational setting would be advantageous.
- Has excellent organisational skills and strong attention to detail.
- Communicates confidently and professionally, both verbally and in writing.
- Is confident using Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel and Outlook.
- Can manage competing priorities and work effectively in a busy environment.
- Demonstrates discretion and understands the importance of confidentiality and data protection.
- Has a friendly, approachable manner and enjoys working as part of a team.
- Is proactive, adaptable and able to use their own initiative.
- Understands the importance of safeguarding and maintaining a safe environment for students.
- Is reliable, punctual and committed to providing a high standard of administrative support.

To join us and be successful in this role you will need to:
- Have experience working within an administrative environment
- Enhanced DBS Disclosure, Overseas Police Clearances (if applicable) and professional reference checks
- CV must cover the full CV History
- Legal right to work in the UK

If you're an experienced or recently qualified Administrative assistant looking for an exciting new opportunity and would like to register with Tradewind Recruitment, please apply now and take the next step in your teaching career! Or for more information about the role, contact Alex Bateman on (phone number removed) / (url removed)

title: Customer Service Support - MK123
description:

title: BOM Administrator
salary_text: £28000 - £30000 per year (Regular days, 37.5 hours per week)
description:
BOM Administrator

Location: Hull, UK

Salary: 28k - 30k

A Manufacturing company is recruiting for the role of a BOM Administrator who will be responsible for the creation and maintenance of an accurate bill of materials for manufacturing and after-sales within project and production timescales.

The ideal candidate will be a highly motivated and organised individual who has can work well under pressure ensuring an excellent standard of attention to detail.

You will have the opportunity to be part of a fast-paced, dynamic environment renowned for innovation, quality construction, stylish design and outstanding value! The Product Development department generate and maintain engineering drawings and bill of materials for every model, hundreds of drawings are created, modified and issued every week.

MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES
- Working with the Product Engineer for each product group to develop an engineering BOM for each model, providing the rest of the company with expertise and technical support.
- Ensure Safety critical and Type Approval components are accurately identified on databases and BOMs.
- Assisting the Project Manager and BOM Team Leader on measuring the progress of projects by compiling and assessing KPI's and Critical Data information.
- Create and maintain bills of material with the aid of the Product Engineer for new products.
- Assess cost, weight and complexity of new models and refine such information during product execution.
- Liaise with other members of the project team to resolve process & operational issues that inhibit effective project delivery.
- Adopt best practice tools & techniques for project information work in order to maximise efficiency and quality of output.
- Link and update parts for the After-sales and IDOL data base systems with the latest data and photographic images.
- Support the D&D Technical Support Team with information and support with direct communication with customers and dealers when requested.
- Compliance with Health & Safety requirements.

QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE
- 5 GCSE or equivalent in English & Math and a high standard of further education (ONC or HNC level preferable)
- Additional qualifications or evidence of training in Data Management would be an advantage
- Familiar with BOM & database tools techniques
- Familiar with Microsoft Office programmes (Excel, Word etc)
- Ability to work under minimum supervision
- Strong problem solving & decision-making skills
- Ability to work well under pressure to achieve deadlines
- High level of accuracy in work and strong attention to detail
- Flexible, adaptable, enthusiastic and motivated
- Excellent verbal & written communication skills

BENEFITS
- 5 hour week
- 27 days annual leave plus 8 bank holidays
- Early finish Friday
- Easy access to site & free on-site parking
- Free Gym Membership

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
As an Accounts Assistant in Hull, you will help keep the accounting and finance function organised by completing day-to-day finance tasks accurately. Your work will support clear financial records for an organisation in the industrial / manufacturing sector.

The organisation operates in the industrial / manufacturing sector in Hull.

title: Logistics Coordinator
description:
Logistics Coordinator

Hull

Permanent Full-time

A well-established logistics business in Hull is looking to appoint a Logistics Coordinator to join its busy operations team.

This position would suit someone who enjoys working in a structured, deadline-led environment and is confident managing moving parts across transport, documentation and operational support. The hours follow a rotating pattern, so flexibility around working times is important.

The opportunity

This role centres around keeping freight movements on track from start to finish, making sure everything is lined up correctly for smooth onward movement. You will be involved in organising load activity, maintaining accurate system records, coordinating with internal departments and helping avoid disruption, delay or unnecessary spend.

Attention to detail is key, particularly where timings, system updates and operational paperwork are concerned.

Responsibilities
- Coordinate daily freight activity to ensure movements are arranged in line with customer and operational requirements
- Keep internal systems updated with accurate movement information and shipment status details
- Make sure vehicle and load activity is prepared in advance to avoid issues at site access points
- Check all operational paperwork is in place and chase anything outstanding before movement takes place
- Work closely with other teams to keep cargo flowing efficiently through the network
- Monitor shipment progress and help resolve issues that could affect service or timing
- Arrange additional operational support such as short-term holding space where required
- Maintain clear and accurate records across shipment references and release information
- Support overall service performance by helping the team meet operational expectations and deadlines

About you
- Previous experience within logistics, freight, shipping, transport coordination or a similar operational environment
- Strong organisational skills and a high level of attention to detail
- Ability to manage live operational information accurately and efficiently
- Comfortable using internal systems and updating records in real time
- Able to work well in a fast-paced environment and respond to changing demands
- Good communication skills with a practical, team-focused approach
- Exposure to import/export activity, freight forwarding, port-related operations or logistics administration would be an advantage

Why join?
- Join an established and growing business
- Long-term stability within a busy logistics operation
- Supportive team environment
- Opportunity to build a long-term career
- Varied role within a fast-paced setting

title: Procurement Coordinator
description:
Procurement Coordinator

Location: Site-based, Hull, HU2 8 QS

Salary: £28,000-£32,000, dependent on experience

Hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00am-5:00pm

Contract: Full-time, permanent

Closing date: Sunday 1st November 2026

About FR Scott

FR Scott is one of Hull's leading independent suppliers of fixings, fasteners, architectural ironmongery, tools and industrial consumables. Established in 1945, we support customers across construction, engineering, manufacturing and modular building from our Hull trade counter, warehouse and national ecommerce operation.

The opportunity

We are looking for an organised, practical person to help keep purchasing and supply running reliably, while supporting the Head of Procurement in developing the wider function.

Day-to-day purchasing, stock availability and supplier coordination are central to this role. Alongside these responsibilities, you will support sourcing, commercial analysis, product and category development, and projects to improve how we buy and manage supply across the business.

FR Scott is a small business. Responsibilities overlap, and we need someone who takes ownership, works closely with colleagues and is willing to provide support and cover where needed. Procurement includes both the products we buy to sell and the goods and services we buy to run the business.

What you'll be doing
- Manage day-to-day purchasing and replenishment, maintaining accurate purchase orders, supplier acknowledgements, costs and delivery dates.
- Follow up outstanding orders and resolve shortages, delivery discrepancies and invoice queries, working closely with Sales, Warehouse and Finance.
- Support supplier sourcing and negotiations by obtaining and comparing quotations, benchmarking prices and identifying opportunities to improve cost, quality and availability.
- Analyse sales, stock, margin and supplier spend to support buying decisions, range reviews and commercial improvements.
- Support inventory and supplier performance reviews, helping address slow-moving stock, availability issues and recurring supply problems.
- Maintain accurate product and supplier information, including specifications, pricing and technical documentation, and support new products and range development for Fix&Fast.
- Contribute to supplier onboarding, purchasing controls, reporting and improvements to procurement processes and digital tools.
- Take responsibility for agreed suppliers, product groups and projects as your knowledge develops, providing support and cover across the wider team.

About you

You may already work in purchasing, buying or supply chain, or have relevant experience in product administration, ecommerce, sales coordination, order management or merchandising. Industry experience would be useful, but it is not essential.
- Strong attention to detail and good organisational skills.
- Confidence communicating with suppliers and colleagues and following actions through.
- Confidence using Excel to analyse sales, stock and purchasing data, compare quotations and maintain accurate records.
- An interest in products, pricing, stock and supplier performance.
- A proactive approach, commercial awareness and willingness to take ownership.

Development and progression

Working directly with the Head of Procurement, you will gain experience across buying, supplier management, stock and category development, with opportunities to take ownership of suppliers, product groups and projects as your skills grow.

This could support progression into Buyer, Category Manager or wider procurement and supply chain roles, depending on your strengths and business opportunities. Support towards a relevant CIPS qualification may be available following successful completion of probation.

What we offer
- £28,000-£32,000 salary, dependent on experience.
- 23 days' annual leave plus bank holidays, increasing with length of service.
- Annual bonus scheme and company pension.
- Employee discount, on-site parking and sick pay.
- Training and development opportunities.

Apply

Apply through this advert with your CV. Applicants must have the right to work in the UK.

Closing date: Sunday 1st November 2026

description:
Facilities Coordinator - 12 Month Fixed-Term Contract Location: Hull, East Yorkshire
Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience
Job Type: Full Time 12 Month FTC
Hours: 35 hours per week
Working Pattern: Hybrid / Agile Working
Travel: Regular travel to UK offices, with occasional overnight stays

An excellent opportunity has arisen for a proactive and organised Facilities Coordinator to join the Facilities team of a well-established and forward-thinking legal services organisation based in Hull.

This is a varied and hands-on position, supporting the day-to-day management, maintenance and smooth running of multiple office locations across the UK.

Working closely with colleagues, landlords, contractors and external suppliers, you will help ensure that offices remain safe, compliant, well-maintained and efficient, while supporting facilities projects, office moves and workplace improvements.

Offering hybrid working, an excellent benefits package and exposure to multi-site facilities management, this opportunity would suit someone who enjoys a varied role combining practical problem-solving, facilities administration and health and safety responsibilities.

The Role As Facilities Coordinator, your responsibilities will include:
- Coordinating day-to-day facilities operations, building maintenance and repairs across multiple UK offices.
- Liaising with landlords, maintenance contractors, suppliers and third-party service providers.
- Supporting workplace health and safety compliance, including risk assessments and workstation assessments.
- Monitoring outstanding actions and ensuring facilities and safety issues are addressed promptly.
- Assisting with office moves, refurbishments, minor maintenance works and facilities improvement projects.
- Maintaining accurate facilities records, compliance documentation and building safety information.
- Supporting the review and development of facilities policies, procedures and processes.
- Managing facilities-related requests and tickets through Salesforce.
- Coordinating and booking complex business travel arrangements.
- Supporting internal and external events and ensuring offices operate effectively.

About You We are looking for a practical, organised and approachable individual who enjoys taking ownership of tasks and ensuring things run smoothly.

Essential requirements:
- Previous experience or a good working knowledge of office health and safety procedures.
- IOSH qualification or currently working towards one.

title: Accounts Receivable Administrator
description:
Role: Accounts Receivable Administrator

Location: Hessle, HU13

Are you a proactive and driven Accounts Receivable Administrator with great communication skills? Can you manage and support company credit control by taking responsibility for your own book of debtor accounts?

Then Scientific Laboratory Supplies (SLS) is the right fit for you. Join us and contribute to our mission of being the UK's largest independent supplier of laboratory equipment, chemicals, and consumables.

We have an exciting opportunity available for a Credit Controller to join our finance team based in Hessle, HU13, on a full-time, permanent basis.

Job Summary:

The Accounts Receivable Administrator will join the SLS Finance team and contribute to all areas within the finance function. The successful candidate will be asked to support the busy credit control function in the office but must be willing to provide support as needed to other areas of the finance function which will include communicating with colleagues, external parties, customers, and vendors.

Key Responsibilities:
- Take a proactive role in managing and supporting company credit control by taking responsibility for own book of debtor accounts.
- Use all forms of communication (email, letters, and telephone) to professionally contact debtors and ensure payment of outstanding invoices.
- Support the ongoing process of credit checking new customers and open new credit accounts ensuring the company has all the relevant information.
- Support and resolve all problems experienced in the credit control function including providing copy invoices, obtaining proof of delivery.
- Work closely with colleagues in Sales and Customer Services to resolve any customer queries and enquiries to progress matters to a satisfactory conclusion.
- Report regularly to the Accounts Office Manager on outstanding issues and promptly inform them of potential debtors' problems.
- When required, help colleagues to manage the "slsledger" email inbox, resolving enquiries quickly and effectively and to pass enquiries onto colleagues in both Finance and other departments for resolution.
- Maintain financial system records and enter data accurately.

Perform general clerical duties when required, including, but not limited to, typing, mailing, filing correspondence and answering telephone calls.

Ideal Candidate:
- Prior experience of working in a credit control / accounts receivable function.
- Comfortable with IT.
- Strong literacy and numeracy skills.
- Interpersonal skills, appreciation of good internal and external customer service behaviour.
- Be organised, methodical, self-motivated, and driven.
- Responsive and re-active.
- Good customer-facing and personal relationship skills.
- Be able to communicate at all levels.
- Ability to work within a flexible team.

About us:

SLS are the UK's largest independent supplier of laboratory equipment, chemicals, and consumables. Because of our independence, we have a unique approach to sourcing and supplying the highest quality, best value products, and brands. Supplying to a wide range of sectors, provides a diverse and interesting customer base as well as providing countless opportunity to grow and expand.

With customers all over the UK, we are a stable and growing company who have an excellent reputation in the market.

We are passionate about our people and have developed a strong team dynamic who are welcoming and supportive of new individuals, joining the company with a brilliant management team to support you as you find your feet in the role.

We are also proud to be a Living Wage Employer and committed to equal opportunities and actively promote a diverse and inclusive working environment, and fairness for everyone.

Alongside our commitment to your professional and personal development, we also offer a generous benefits package including:
- Competitive salary
- 25 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays
- Company pension
- Enhanced Maternity and Paternity leave
- Small, friendly, and sociable teams with staff events
- Company profit bonus schemes
- Cycle 2work schemes
- Career opportunities for development and progression

title: Visits Receptionist
description:
Visits Receptionist

Location: East Riding of Yorkshire

Salary: £26,000 per annum

About The Role

Forward Trust is a social justice charity supporting thousands of people to overcome addiction and mental health challenges, move away from crime, secure employment and housing, and build a positive sense of belonging.

We are passionate about challenging stigma and changing public attitudes and policy, ensuring that people who are often overlooked by society have access to the support and opportunities they need to transform their lives.

As the UK s leading addiction recovery charity, we bring expertise in recovery, reducing reoffending, homelessness and employment support, helping people recognise their potential and build a better future.

About HMP Millsike

HMP Millsike is committed to a modern, evidence-based approach to prison delivery, combining public protection with a strong focus on rehabilitation and personal development.

At the heart of Millsike is a culture that empowers individuals to make positive choices, develop essential life skills and build the emotional resilience needed to achieve lasting change.

Through partnership working, research and innovative approaches to resettlement, HMP Millsike aims to become a leader in reducing reoffending and creating meaningful opportunities for people leaving prison. A key ambition is to ensure that at least 26% of prisoners move directly into employment on release.

What we are looking for

We are looking for people who are passionate about making a positive difference in the lives of others and who believe that everyone deserves the opportunity to change and succeed.

The ideal candidate will:
- Share Forward Trust s values and commitment to social justice, rehabilitation and recovery.
- Believe in the potential of people to change, regardless of their background or past experiences.
- Demonstrate empathy, compassion and a non-judgemental approach.
- Have strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build positive, professional relationships.
- Be committed to promoting equality, diversity, inclusion and individual choice.
- Be able to motivate and encourage individuals to recognise their strengths and work towards their goals.
- Demonstrate resilience, professionalism and the ability to work effectively in a challenging environment.
- Work collaboratively with colleagues and partner organisations to achieve positive outcomes.
- Be organised, reliable and committed to delivering high-quality support.
- Understand the importance of safeguarding, professional boundaries and maintaining confidentiality.
- Be passionate about helping people develop the skills, confidence and opportunities needed to lead positive, independent lives.

Joining Forward Trust means becoming part of an organisation that believes in second chances and the power of people to transform their lives.

You will have the opportunity to:
- Make a meaningful difference to people s lives and futures.
- Be part of a team committed to rehabilitation, recovery and reducing reoffending.
- Help create opportunities for people to access employment, housing and community support.
- Contribute to a progressive prison environment focused on positive change and long-term outcomes.
- Support a wider mission to challenge stigma, promote social justice and help people build fulfilling lives.
- Together, we can help people move forward, rebuild their lives and create lasting change.

About Us

We are The Forward Trust, the social enterprise with charitable status that empowers people to break the often interlinked cycles of crime and addiction to move forward with their lives. For more than 25 years we have been working with people to build positive and productive lives, whatever their past. We believe that anyone is capable of lasting change. Our services have supported thousands of people to make positive changes and build productive lives with a job, family, friends and a sense of community.

Please note that we may close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of suitable applications.

Please note that remote roles may require occasional travel for site visits, training and meetings.

To Apply

If you feel you are a suitable candidate and would like to work for Forward Trust, please click apply to be redirected to our website to complete your application.

description:

Are you immediately available and able to work in a temporary contract for a well established business who need additional support to process a backlog of work in the first instance.

Our client, a well-established and growing manufacturer based in the Bridlington area, is seeking a temporary Bookkeeper to join their team and support them with a backlog of accounts work.

They are looking for an enthusiastic individual to take on a crucial role, providing essential financial support and contributing to the smooth operation of the business.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone with solid bookkeeping experience, particularly with Sage, who is eager to become an integral part of a hands-on SME.

What the Bookkeeper job involves

You ll play a key role in managing the daily financial operations, ensuring accuracy and efficiency.
- Raising customer invoices and delivery notes on a daily basis.
- Managing the invoice factoring process.
- Daily monitoring of bank accounts and cashflow.
- Payroll administration, collating employee hours each week from a clocking in system and send to payroll.
- Matching invoices and accurately allocating payments within Sage.

This is a varied and fast-paced role that would suit someone who enjoys being at the heart of an operational team, managing multiple financial priorities, and providing excellent administrative support.

Skills required

We re looking for candidates who can demonstrate a practical approach and a willingness to contribute beyond traditional bookkeeping duties. Ideal candidates will have:
- Proven experience with Sage 50 would be beneficial.
- The ability to manage and allocate payments efficiently within Sage.
- Self managed and able to work on their own initiative.
- A high degree of adaptability and flexibility to take on a range of tasks as needed.

title: Sales Coordinator
description:
Futures are recruiting a Business Development Advisor to support our clients sales activity and help create a positive experience for prospective and existing customers. You ll be one of the first points of contact for incoming enquiries, gathering relevant information and making sure each enquiry is handled promptly and professionally.

Working closely with sales and marketing teams, you ll help keep customer information organised, support business development and telesales activity, and follow company processes throughout.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Responding to incoming customer enquiries by telephone and other channels
- Speaking with prospective and existing customers to understand their needs and record relevant details
- Supporting business development and telesales activity through clear, confident communication
- Coordinating with sales and marketing colleagues to help manage enquiries and share relevant customer information
- Keeping customer records accurate and current in the company s CRM system
- Using research skills to gather information that supports customer conversations and business development work
- Using Microsoft Office and CRM systems to record, organise and update information
- Following company processes and contributing to a consistent, professional customer experience

The Ideal Candidate
- Strong telephone manner and communication skills
- Good research and organisational skills
- Confidence using Microsoft Office and CRM systems
- GCSEs in Maths and English
- A valid driving licence and access to transport

You ll be proactive, professional and able to work collaboratively with colleagues across sales and marketing. If you enjoy customer contact and can combine confident communication with careful organisation, we d like to hear from you.

title: Administration Assistant
description: " Please note that this advertised vacancy does not meet the UKVI eligibility requirements for a Skilled Worker Visa and therefore HTFT would not be able to issue a Certificate of Sponsorship for this role." An opportunity has arisen for a full-time Band 2 Administration Assistant to work within our Mental Health Crisis Team based at Miranda House in Hull. You will be expected to be flexible and work in a fast paced and highly demanding environment within the main office as well as providing cover to a very busy reception area. The administration team provides 24 hour, 7 day a week cover which is worked on a rota basis incorporating enhanced pay for unsocial hours. This provides a refreshing work life balance. This role involves liaising with health care professionals from the Trust and outside agencies, also dealing with queries from patients requiring a service. Excellent interpersonal skills and being able to work on own initiative are both essential. The successful candidate will have good keyboard skills enabling them to assist in creating, developing and maintaining new processes and procedures. This includes regular data inputting using patient systems (Systm One ) in accordance with the Trust standards. Along with all other Microsoft Packages. Applicants will have RSA III and OCRIII/ECDL or equivalent NVQ Qualification, a good standard of Maths and English and have previous experience of carrying out general administrative procedures in an office environment. Experience of using software packages including Microsoft Word/Outlook and Excel are beneficial. Experience with the Trust Patient Information Systems (Systm One ) would be advantageous. For further details with regard to this vacancy opportunity, please see the attached Job Description and Person Specification.
